newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African fuel taxes, rebates change in budget.
newsitem.headline: S.African fuel taxes, rebates change in budget.

text.p: The government would scrap the diesel refund system and continue reducing subsidies paid to the synthetic fuels industry, the finance department said on Wednesday.
This would yield an additional 800 million rand in 1997/98, the department's budget review released with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's budget speech said.
It said that the equalisation fund, which is used to subsidise Sasol Ltd and state-run Mossgas, was over-funded and it had been decided to speed up the phasing out of the subsidy announced last year.
As a result, the equalisation fund levy would be cut by four cents a litre for petrol and 2.5 cents a litre for diesel as from April 2, while the fuel levy would be increased by the same amounts.
This would have no effect on the pump price of fuel.
The whole issue of subsidies for the synthetic fuels industry was still being examined by a special cabinet committee, the review said.
The diesel refund system allows for the partial refund of excise duty and fuel levies paid on diesel used in agriculture, forestry and related road and rail transport.
Since March 1992, the refund has been 3.63 cents per litre in excise duty and 16.96 cents per litre in fuel levy, or 20.6 cents a litre total.
"Experience has shown that the refund system is open to abuse," the review said.
Measures to control the system had been costly and ineffective and in view of the 19 cents cut in the diesel price on March 5, it had been decided to drop the refund system immediately.
